alerts.quote: Starting January 6, 2025, all new apps submitted to the Shopify App Store must use the [new GraphQL Product APIs](https://shopify.dev/changelog/new-graphql-product-apis-that-support-up-to-2000-variants-now-available-in-2024-04).

alerts.summary: All public apps, including those already listed in the Shopify App Store, must migrate to the new GraphQL Product APIs by February 1, 2025.
alerts.quote: As of February 1, 2025, all public apps must migrate to the [new GraphQL Product APIs](https://shopify.dev/changelog/new-graphql-product-apis-that-support-up-to-2000-variants-now-available-in-2024-04).

alerts.summary: Migrate the deprecated CartBuyerIdentity.deliveryAddressPreferences output and removed CartBuyerIdentityInput.deliveryAddressPreferences input to the new cart delivery-address model and mutations, supplying deliveryAddresses where required.
alerts.quote: As of API version 2025-01, the [`deliveryAddressPreferences`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/storefront/2025-01/objects/CartBuyerIdentity#field-deliveryaddresspreferences) field on the `CartBuyerIdentity` object is deprecated.

alerts.summary: Fetching fulfillment holds through node or nodes returns null for holds on inaccessible fulfillment orders; request the appropriate fulfillment-order access scopes before migrating to 2025-01 and handle null results.
alerts.quote: As of the Admin API version 2025-01, apps using the [node or nodes GraphQL queries](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/objects/FulfillmentHold#interface-node) to fetch fulfillment holds will only be able to fetch those that belong to a fulfillment order that they have access to.

alerts.summary: Customer-containing webhook payloads no longer include `tags`; update consumers to track changes through the `customer.tags_added` and `customer.tags_removed` webhooks.
alerts.quote: * We removed `tags` in favour of the `customer.tags_added` and `customer.tags_removed` webhooks.

alerts.summary: Customer-containing webhook payloads no longer include `email_marketing_consent`; update consumers to receive consent changes through `customers/email_marketing_consent_update`.
alerts.quote: * We removed `email_marketing_consent` in favour of the `customers/email_marketing_consent_update`.

alerts.summary: Customer-containing webhook payloads no longer include `sms_marketing_consent`; update consumers to receive consent changes through `customers/marketing_consent_update`.
alerts.quote: * We removed `sms_marketing_consent` in favour of the `customers/marketing_consent_update`.

alerts.summary: Customer-containing webhook payloads no longer include `last_order_id`, `last_order_name`, `total_spent`, or `orders_count`; consume the purchasing summary webhook for the available fields and remove reliance on `last_order_name`, which has no stated replacement.
alerts.quote: * We removed the following fields: `last_order_id`, `last_order_name`, `total_spent`, and `orders_count`. They are now available in the new `customers/purchasing_summary` webhook except for `last_order_name` being deprecated.

alerts.summary: FulfillmentOrderSortKeys.RELEVANCE is no longer valid; update affected queries and variables to use a supported sort key appropriate to the intended ordering.
alerts.quote: Starting in API version **2025-01**, RELEVANCE will be removed as a valid value from [FulfillmentOrderSortKeys](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2024-10/enums/FulfillmentOrderSortKeys) in the GraphQL Admin API.

alerts.summary: FulfillmentOrder.fulfillmentHolds now returns all active holds, so update code that assumes a fulfillment order has at most one hold.
alerts.quote: As of the `2025-01` API version, the [fulfillmentOrder.fulfillmentHolds field](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/objects/FulfillmentOrder#field-fulfillmentholds) now returns all active holds applied to a fulfillment order.

alerts.summary: fulfillmentOrderHold can now succeed on an already-held order, so review retry and duplicate-hold handling, supply unique handles for additional holds, and omit fulfillmentOrderLineItems when the order is already held.
alerts.quote: As of the `2025-01` API version, the [fulfillmentOrderHold mutation](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/mutations/fulfillmentOrderHold) can now be successfully executed on fulfillment orders that are already on hold.

alerts.summary: supportedActions can now include HOLD for an already-held fulfillment order, so do not treat that action as evidence that the order is not on hold.
alerts.quote: The [fulfillmentOrder.supportedActions](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/objects/fulfillmentorder#field-supportedactions) field will now return the [HOLD](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/enums/FulfillmentOrderAction#value-hold) action when a fulfillment order is on hold and an additional hold can be added.

alerts.summary: Releasing holds without holdIds releases every hold and can prematurely fulfill items; use API version 2024-10 or newer and explicitly select the hold IDs to release.
alerts.quote: Releasing all holds on a fulfillment order without supplying the hold IDs will result in the fulfillment order being released prematurely and items being incorrectly fulfilled.

alerts.summary: The fulfillment_orders/placed_on_hold webhook payload can contain multiple fulfillment_holds, so update handlers that assume a single hold.
alerts.quote: As of the `2025-01` API version, now that a fulfillment order can have multiple holds, the `fulfillment_order.fulfillment_holds` field in the [fulfillment\_orders/placed\_on\_hold](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/webhooks?reference=toml#list-of-topics-fulfillment_orders/placed_on_hold) webhook payload can now return multiple holds.

alerts.summary: REST fulfillment-order responses expose only the oldest active hold and cannot represent all holds, so migrate hold-reading logic to GraphQL 2025-01 or newer when complete visibility is required.
alerts.quote: The [fulfillment holds attribute on the fulfilment order resource](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-rest/2025-01/resources/fulfillmentorder) will continue showing only the one oldest active hold under scenarios of multiple holds.

alerts.summary: The REST release-hold endpoint releases all holds and can prematurely release an order, so migrate to GraphQL fulfillmentOrderReleaseHold and explicitly select hold IDs.
alerts.quote: The [release hold endpoint](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-rest/2025-01/resources/fulfillmentorder#post-fulfillment-orders-fulfillment-order-id-release-hold) will continue to release the fulfillment order from being held by releasing it from all holds at once.

alerts.summary: Storefront Cart tax and duty fields are deprecated; stop relying on cart-level tax and duty estimates and use the amounts finalized at Checkout.
alerts.quote: As of API version `2025-01`, we're deprecating the [tax and duty](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/storefront/2024-01/objects/Cart#field-cost) fields in Storefront API Cart.

alerts.summary: Product creation and updates now reject duplicate handles; ensure explicitly supplied handles are unique when calling productCreate, productUpdate, or productSet.
alerts.quote: As of the `2025-01` version of the Admin GraphQL API, the `handle` field in [productInput](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/input-objects/ProductInput) for [productCreate](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/productCreate) and [productUpdate](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/productUpdate), as well as in [productSetInput](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/input-objects/ProductSetInput) for [productSet](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/latest/mutations/productSet) will be validated for uniqueness.

alerts.summary: SubscriptionMailingAddress is deprecated in Admin API 2025-07; update affected queries, fragments and generated types to use MailingAddress.
alerts.quote: As of the 2025-07 version of the GraphQL Admin API, we've deprecated the [`SubscriptionMailingAddress`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/objects/SubscriptionMailingAddress) object.

alerts.summary: Only ONLINE_STORE is accepted for ScriptTagInput.displayScope, and scriptTagCreate defaults to ONLINE_STORE when it is omitted; update callers that use other values or rely on the previous default.
alerts.quote: As of Admin GraphQL API version 2025-01, the only valid value for the `displayScope` field on the [`ScriptTagInput` object](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/unstable/input-objects/ScriptTagInput) is `ONLINE_STORE`.

alerts.summary: Script tags stop working on the Order status page on August 28, 2025; migrate affected functionality to UI extensions.
alerts.quote: This change is related to Script tags being turned off for the Order status page on August 28, 2025, following the launch of [UI Extensions on the Thank You and Order status pages](https://shopify.dev/changelog/ui-extensions-on-the-thank-you-and-order-status-pages-have-launched).

alerts.summary: Stop relying on CalculatedOrder for committed order edits or its deprecated committed field; use Order for current state and Order.agreements for past changes, while retaining CalculatedOrder for uncommitted edits.
alerts.quote: * **January 1, 2026 (version `2026-01`):** `CalculatedOrders` for committed order edits will no longer be returned. Note: If usage drops to zero before `2026-01`, we may stop returning `CalculatedOrders` in an earlier version.

alerts.summary: Across all API versions, PRIVATE permissions are removed and existing app-reserved data becomes merchant-readable, while all metafields and metaobjects become accessible in Liquid; review privacy assumptions and update permission handling.
alerts.quote: * On **Feb 1, 2025**, **across all API versions**, we will fully remove **private** permissions for [app-reserved metafields and metaobjects](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/custom-data/reserved-prefixes). **We will migrate all existing metafields and metaobjects** to be merchant readable automatically. All metafields and metaobjects will also become accessible in liquid.

alerts.summary: Across all API versions, PUBLIC_READ and PUBLIC_READ_WRITE permissions are removed and existing app-reserved data becomes accessible only to the owning app and merchant; update permission handling and review integrations relying on public access.
alerts.quote: * On **Apr 1, 2025**, **across all API versions**, we will fully remove **public** permissions for [app-reserved metafields and metaobjects](https://shopify.dev/docs/apps/build/custom-data/reserved-prefixes).**We will migrate all existing metafields and metaobjects** to be only accessible by your app and the merchant automatically.

alerts.summary: The REST Admin product image resource is deprecated as of 2025-01; migrate affected calls to GraphQL using media IDs.
alerts.quote: As of `2025-01`, the admin REST API for the [product image resource](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-rest/2024-10/resources/product-image) is now deprecated.

alerts.summary: Discounts Allocator Functions no longer run, and retaining purchase.discounts-allocator.run blocks deployment of the entire app; remove that extension from app configuration and redeploy.
alerts.quote: Until you remove it, `shopify app deploy` fails for the entire app, including changes to your other extensions, with `API not found for target: purchase.discounts-allocator.run`.

alerts.summary: Legacy refund mutations are deprecated for return processing; migrate return-related refund and exchange workflows to returnProcess rather than simply renaming calls.
alerts.quote: * The [`returnRefund`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-07/mutations/returnRefund) mutation is deprecated and replaced by the new [`returnProcess`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-07/mutations/returnProcess) mutation. The [`returnProcess`](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-07/mutations/returnProcess) mutation streamlines return lifecycle management by combining disposition decisions and financial processing into a single call.

alerts.summary: Exchange fulfillment orders are created only when exchange line items are processed; update return-creation and approval workflows to call returnProcess before expecting those orders.
alerts.quote: * Exchange fulfillment orders are now created only when exchange line items are processed, ensuring accuracy.

alerts.summary: Only exchanges with a net balance payable by the buyer receive an AWAITING_PAYMENT hold; update logic that assumes all exchanges receive that hold.
alerts.quote: * Only exchanges with a net payable balance due by the buyer are placed on hold with `AWAITING_PAYMENT` hold reason.

alerts.summary: Older API versions return null for imperial units and counts in unit pricing; update unit-pricing requests to API version 2025-07 and handle the new units.
alerts.quote: Otherwise, the API will return the price value but return `null` imperial units and counts.

alerts.summary: Older API versions return null for imperial units and counts in unit pricing; update unit-pricing requests to API version 2025-07 and handle the new units.
alerts.quote: Otherwise, the API will return the price value but return `null` imperial units and counts.

alerts.summary: Automatic discount minimum requirements can now be null; handle null values when reading DiscountAutomaticBasic.minimumRequirement and DiscountAutomaticFreeShipping.minimumRequirement.
alerts.quote: As of version 2025-01, the `minimumRequirement` field for both [DiscountAutomaticBasic](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/objects/DiscountAutomaticBasic#field-minimumrequirement) and [DiscountAutomaticFreeShipping](https://shopify.dev/docs/api/admin-graphql/2025-01/objects/DiscountAutomaticFreeShipping#field-minimumrequirement) will become nullable.

alerts.summary: ReverseFulfillmentOrder.order can now return null instead of a GraphQL error when the order is unavailable; handle null before accessing order fields.
alerts.quote: As of **2025-01**, `ReverseFulfillmentOrder.order` field is nullable.

alerts.summary: Requests must use a spec-compliant JSON body and Content-Type: application/json; replace legacy application/graphql bodies and missing or unsupported content types to avoid HTTP 415 responses.
alerts.quote: * The `Content-Type` header *must* specify `application/json`. The legacy `application/graphql` request format is no longer supported. Requests with no supported content type will receive a `415 Unsupported Media Type` response.

alerts.summary: Requests must use a spec-compliant JSON body and Content-Type: application/json; replace legacy application/graphql bodies and missing or unsupported content types to avoid HTTP 415 responses.
alerts.quote: * The `Content-Type` header *must* specify `application/json`. The legacy `application/graphql` request format is no longer supported. Requests with no supported content type will receive a `415 Unsupported Media Type` response.

alerts.summary: Requests with no supported Accept media type now receive HTTP 406; send an Accept header supporting application/json or application/graphql-response+json.
alerts.quote: * The `Accept` header now supports `application/graphql-response+json` and/or `application/json` response formats. Requests with no supported accept types will receive a `406 Not Acceptable` response.

alerts.summary: Requests with no supported Accept media type now receive HTTP 406; send an Accept header supporting application/json or application/graphql-response+json.
alerts.quote: * The `Accept` header now supports `application/graphql-response+json` and/or `application/json` response formats. Requests with no supported accept types will receive a `406 Not Acceptable` response.

alerts.summary: On /graphql, Accept: */* now selects application/graphql-response+json, which returns HTTP 400 for static validation failures instead of HTTP 200; update response handling or explicitly request application/json to retain the previous format.
alerts.quote: * Accepting `*/*` will default to a `application/graphql-response+json` response.

alerts.summary: On /graphql, Accept: */* now selects application/graphql-response+json, which returns HTTP 400 for static validation failures instead of HTTP 200; update response handling or explicitly request application/json to retain the previous format.
alerts.quote: * Accepting `*/*` will default to a `application/graphql-response+json` response.

alerts.summary: Admin GraphQL requests using application/graphql are rejected in API versions 2025-01 and later; use Content-Type: application/json and a GraphQL-over-HTTP JSON-encoded request body.
alerts.quote: The `Content-Type: application/graphql` request format is deprecated and will no longer be accepted as of 2025-01 schema versions.

alerts.summary: Customer Account API requests using application/graphql are rejected in API versions 2025-01 and later; use Content-Type: application/json and a GraphQL-over-HTTP JSON-encoded request body.
alerts.quote: The `Content-Type: application/graphql` request format is deprecated and will no longer be accepted as of 2025-01 schema versions.
